newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong handover dominates British press.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong handover dominates British press.

text.p: The British press marked Hong Kong's handover to China with blanket coverage and catchy headlines on Tuesday, and one newspaper bid farewell with a headline in Chinese characters.
"It all ends in tears," trumpeted the Express, reporting the departing governor Chris Patten's farewell address.
The Express highlighted the torrential downpour that dominated the proceedings.
"Britain's rule of Hong Kong ended last night in a crashing, thunderous storm. Was it an omen, we all wondered?"

The Independent headlined its coverage with "Goodbye Hong Kong" spelled out in Chinese characters beneath a front page photograph of troops from China's People's Liberation Army crossing the border into Hong Kong.
"China's new top brass sweep in like emperors," said another Independent headline.
The Daily Telegraph said the concept of "one country, two systems" would be a good test of Beijing's political maturity.
"An inability to refrain from interfering in Hong Kong will demonstrate that China, despite its rapid economic growth, remains a fundamentally crude and backward country," it said.
The Guardian welcomed the promise by Hong Kong's new chief executive, Tung Chee-hwa, to move quickly towards electing a new legislature.
It said Britain had a clear obligation to continue to monitor the progress of the agreement with China on the future of Hong Kong.
"The greatest betrayal would be if, after all the eulogies to Hong Kong's way of life, the outside world lost interest because there were no dramatic upheavals - and walked quietly away," it said.
